title: The Biased Oracle: Assessing LLMs’ Understandability and Empathy in Medical Diagnoses

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring variations in readability metrics and LLM-as-a-judge/human empathy ratings for diagnostic explanations generated across four patient age groups (<18, 18-49, 50-64, 65+).
Assessing changes in text readability complexity and empathy scores across different patient education levels (high school or lower, university degree, medical degree).
Evaluating readability and empathy scores of diagnostic outputs when prompting the models with different patient geographical backgrounds (European, African, Asian).
Comparing text understandability and empathy evaluations of diagnostic explanations generated for male versus female patients.
Analyzing how different health diagnoses (obesity, pancreatic cancer, Alzheimer's, chronic ischemic heart disease) influence the readability and empathy of the generated medical explanations.
Measuring intra-model bias by comparing how an LLM rates the empathy of its own generated responses versus responses generated by a different model using an LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline.
